My smart lock has been in use for five to six years, and I have tried quite a few options during that time. The ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid choice for nearly any user, offering Apple Home integration, built-in Wi-Fi, and multiple methods for locking and unlocking. Whether you want to use fingerprint recognition or simply a PIN code, this lock pretty much covers all the bases.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Supports Apple Home, but not Home Key

ULTRALOQ calls the Bolt Fingerprint the first smart lock to be fully integrated with Apple Home, and that integration is exactly what drew me in. Honestly, I still really miss Touch ID on the iPhone. You can lock and unlock it through the Home app or Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV set up as a hub, it can participate in automations and scenes just like any other Apple Home accessory, with remote control support.

Still, there's one feature missing for me: Home Key support. Being able to unlock with just a quick tap using an iPhone or Apple Watch would truly take this lock to the next level. That's the only feature it lacks, but it's not a deal-breaker.

I'm hoping ULTRALOQ will add this feature in future models, because with Home Key, this lock would go from good to nearly perfect. It also supports Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT, so no matter which smart home platform you prefer or might switch to in the future, you have plenty of flexibility. It runs on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, so you don't need an extra bridge to handle basic remote control through its app.

More ways to unlock than you need

The Bolt Fingerprint is certainly not short on ways to unlock. Fingerprint recognition can store up to 50 fingers and up to 50 codes, you can unlock via the phone app, have it automatically unlock as you approach the door, or use voice unlock through Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. Two physical keys are also included, so even if the batteries die, you won't be completely locked out. For me, no physical key option is a complete non-starter.

You can also create up to 50 custom codes, then distribute one-time or time-limited codes to friends, guests, or cleaning staff, among others. If you have a rental property, this feature alone makes it worth considering.

There's also a Lockout mode that temporarily disables all electronic unlock methods, including codes and app access, which is handy for adding an extra layer of security to an empty home while you're travelling. I had never thought about this feature on a smart lock before, but it's not a bad thing to have.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

I've installed quite a few smart door locks over the past few years, and at this point I'm pretty familiar with the process. With the right tools, it can be done in roughly ten minutes. Assuming you're swapping out a modern deadbolt, no wiring or drilling is needed. All you need is a Phillips screwdriver, and you'll also need to replace the strike plate on the door frame.

Once the lock scans and joins your Apple Home setup, and gets assigned to a room, you can control it through the Home app, or include it in automations and scenes so multiple actions trigger at once, such as the lights turning on the moment the door is unlocked.

Wrapping up the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint

Overall, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a great choice for anyone who doesn't need Home Key support. Fingerprint unlock will likely become your go-to method on a daily basis. Installation is also very straightforward. I've had it on my office door for a while now, as there are often laptops sitting in boxes waiting to be configured, and I wanted an extra layer of security. I really like that it automatically unlocks as I approach, and that it can keep track of who's been coming and going. The fingerprint support takes me back to the days of Touch ID.

You can buy the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ website.
